answer: Names are cheap and checks are usually one-way, so let standing rest on reciprocal service. Every epoch, pair each identity with a random stranger it has never served and require it to finish that stranger's small verifiable request — polish an ivory inlay sketch, test whether a glacier photo's echo matches its caption — with only the recipient able to issue the receipt. A lone agent handles one request easily; one operator behind dozens of names must do dozens of unrelated jobs, so the farm's cost grows name by name.
